description: Collection-side diagnostics for arex exporter availability, polling, credentials, eAPI behavior and process resources.

panels.description: Presence of arex_build_info for the selected jobs. If absent, switch poll and command panels are not evidence of a switch failure.
panels.title: Exporter present

panels.description: Unique switches represented by poll-health metrics across the selected jobs.
panels.title: Monitored switches

panels.description: Switches whose last complete poll failed. Check exporter presence before treating an empty panel as switch health.

targets.expr: sum(max by (job, switch) (arista_scrape_success{job=~"$job",switch=~"$switch"}) == bool 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Poll failures

panels.description: Maximum age of the last successful poll. This is informational because each deployment chooses its staleness limit.
panels.title: Oldest successful data

panels.description: Current per-command failures. A command can fail while the overall switch poll succeeds.

targets.expr: sum(min by (job, switch, command) (arista_command_success{job=~"$job",switch=~"$switch"}) == bool 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Failed commands

panels.description: Share of eAPI request rate caused by per-command retry fallback over the last five minutes.
panels.title: Retry share

panels.description: Build identity reported by each selected arex exporter, including version, revision, Go version and VCS build metadata.
panels.title: Deployed versions

panels.description: Commands currently failing by switch. Rows here can coexist with a successful overall poll; no rows means no reported command failure.
panels.title: Failed commands

panels.description: Last complete poll result over time: green is successful and red is failed. Red with a running exporter points toward switch, credential or transport failure; missing data with an absent exporter points to the exporter or scrape path.
panels.title: Poll health by switch

panels.description: Seconds since each switch last completed a successful poll. The configured staleness limit is deployment-specific, so no fixed threshold is applied.
panels.title: Successful data age

panels.description: Request counters shown as five-minute rates. Batch is the normal request; retry is the per-command fallback after a batch failure.
panels.title: eAPI request rate by outcome and attempt

panels.description: Batch and retry request rates remain separately visible. Retry traffic represents amplification from per-command fallback.
panels.title: Retry amplification: batch vs retry rate

panels.description: Mean only: request-duration rate divided by request rate. The catalogue has duration totals, not a histogram, so this is not p95 or p99 latency.
panels.title: Mean eAPI request latency

panels.description: Five-minute rate of eAPI response bytes received from each switch.
panels.title: Response bandwidth by switch

panels.description: Password-file reload events per Grafana rate interval. Rotated, unchanged and failed outcomes use increases rather than raw counters.
panels.title: Credential reload outcomes

panels.description: Exporter-process RSS and live Go heap, grouped by job. Heap is part of RSS, so the series are deliberately not stacked; neither equals Kubernetes pod working-set memory.

targets.expr: sum by (job) (process_resident_memory_bytes{job=~"$job"} and on (job, instance) arex_build_info{job=~"$job"})
sum by (job) (go_memstats_heap_alloc_bytes{job=~"$job"} and on (job, instance) arex_build_info{job=~"$job"})

panels.title: Process memory by job

panels.description: Total goroutines and garbage-collection cycles per second across active exporter instances, grouped by job.

targets.expr: sum by (job) (go_goroutines{job=~"$job"} and on (job, instance) arex_build_info{job=~"$job"})
sum by (job) (rate(go_gc_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job"}[5m]) and on (job, instance) arex_build_info{job=~"$job"})

panels.title: Runtime activity by job

panels.description: CPU cores consumed by arex processes across active exporter instances, grouped by job. This excludes sidecars and other pod overhead.

targets.expr: sum by (job) (rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job=~"$job"}[5m]) and on (job, instance) arex_build_info{job=~"$job"})

panels.title: Exporter CPU by job

panels.description: Kubernetes working-set memory for all real containers in selected arex pods, compared with their summed requests and limits. Requires namespace and pod labels on arex_build_info, plus cAdvisor and kube-state-metrics.
panels.title: Pod memory vs resources

panels.description: Kubernetes CPU cores used by all real containers in selected arex pods, compared with their summed requests and limits. A missing limit line means no CPU limit is configured.
panels.title: Pod CPU vs resources

panels.description: Current Kubernetes pod working-set memory as a percentage of the summed configured container memory limits.

defaults.noValue: No memory limit configured or Kubernetes metrics unavailable

panels.title: Memory limit utilization by pod

panels.description: Current Kubernetes pod CPU usage as a percentage of the summed configured container CPU limits. The default arex chart has no CPU limit, so this panel is empty until one is configured.

defaults.noValue: No CPU limit configured or Kubernetes metrics unavailable

panels.title: CPU limit utilization by pod

panels.description: Top switches by current response bandwidth and eAPI request time accumulated over the selected dashboard range.
panels.title: Expensive switches

title: arex / Exporter health
